reviewer: Codex independent biology Q1 image counterreview

records.science: The conventional parent couple and central descent to three present children are coherent. Two unshaded parents and one shaded affected daughter are possible under recessive inheritance; the drawing does not claim a unique mode or numeric risk. The dashed fourth child is speculative, but a circle preassigns female sex and the dashed sibling link is not a standard neutral pedigree convention.
records.visual: The PNG is RGBA with genuinely transparent background. On an opaque cream inspection composite, symbols and connections are clear at 680 and 360px. On a dark 360px composite, the central parent-to-child and sibling lines and the dashed possible-child link nearly disappear. GoalBookView.tsx renders images in a dark slate figure in dark mode, so the loss is real in this app.
records.requiredCorrection: Generate or edit this candidate as an opaque warm-cream PNG with dark connection lines visible in both themes. Prefer a neutral unknown-sex future-child symbol or an explicitly separate question mark, without an ambiguous dashed sibling edge. Reinspect actual replacement at original, 680 and 360px before binding.

records.science: DNA is wrapped around bead-like histone cores; small marks sit on exposed histone tails rather than on DNA. Dense and open chromatin arrangements are distinct. Both orange and violet marks appear without a false universal claim that methylation always activates or silences. This is a simplified structural aid, not a map from each mark to a fixed gene-expression outcome.
records.visual: At original, 680 and 360px, the labels dicht/locker, nucleosome zoom, tail marks and contrasting packing remain recognizable. Opaque cream background and comic palette align with the biology image landscape.
records.limit: Orange/violet dots are not self-labelled as acetyl/methyl; alt text and teaching context must identify the two mark types and explain context dependence. The image alone does not establish regulation direction or independent learner performance.

records.science: The left panel shows intact mRNA being translated into protein. The right shows duplex siRNA entering a RISC-like complex, one retained guide paired to target mRNA, target mRNA separated into fragments and reduced protein output. This is a plausible siRNA/Argonaute slicing route; it must be described as one RNAi example, not every RNAi pathway.
records.visual: mRNA and siRNA labels, guide/target pairing, the cut and faded output remain distinguishable at 680 and 360px. Opaque warm background and simple comic shapes are consistent with current image style.
records.limit: RISC/Argonaute is represented by an unlabeled green complex; the alt text should name it. A paper source supports siRNA guide-dependent mRNA cleavage, but generation does not prove an active V binding.

records.science: One guide RNA is shown held by Cas9 and paired with an unwound DNA target adjacent to a marked PAM. Opposing arrows indicate cleavage of both DNA strands; the right state consists of two separated double-stranded DNA ends. No automatic precise repair or altered organism is shown. This is a simplified Cas9 cut example rather than a complete editing outcome.
records.visual: Cas9, guide-RNA, DNA and PAM labels and the double-strand cut remain legible at original, 680 and 360px. The opaque friendly comic presentation matches the existing biology landscape.
records.limit: The exact nucleotide sequence and exact base-pair cut offset are intentionally abstracted, so the figure supports the principle only. Alt text should not claim an exact sequence, universal PAM or guaranteed precise edit.
